newsitem.title: FRANCE: Galliano named designer at Christian Dior.
newsitem.headline: Galliano named designer at Christian Dior.

text.p: French fashion house Christian Dior, one of the world's most prestigious labels, announced on Monday the appointment of Britain's flamboyant John Galliano as its new designer.
"The board of directors of Christian Dior approved this morning the appointment of Mr John Galliano to create its haute couture and women's ready-to-wear collections," the firm said in a statement.

Galliano, 36, whose appointment had been widely predicted within the industry, will leave his position at Givenchy to replace Italy's Gianfranco Ferre, who presented his final collection for Christian Dior last Tuesday.
Ferre had worked for the house since 1989.
"We are very happy to have a talent like John Galliano," Dior spokesman Bernard Danillon told Reuters.
Galliano shifts to Dior just one year after moving to Givenchy, where he replaced the house's founder Hubert de Givenchy. Both houses belong to luxury goods giant LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton.
Galliano will design two ready-to-wear and two haute couture collections per year for Dior. He will continue designing for his own label as well.
His first collection for the house, the 1997 Spring Summer haute couture, will be presented in January to celebrate the 50th anniverary of Christian Dior's post-war "New Look".
Galliano's successor at Givenchy would be announced later on Monday, a spokesman said.

During his year at Givenchy, Galliano transformed the house's strait-laced, linear clothes into some of the most romantic and imaginative creations in Paris, pushing down the age of its clientele by decades.
Galliano's romantic aesthetic is closer to the New Look created by Christian Dior himself in 1947, with its sculpted bosom and spreading skirts.
His switch to Dior is expected to give the house an injection of new youthful energy and is part of a strategy by LVMH chief Bernard Arnault to bring fashion's most creative talents into his empire.

Galliano's appointment was also seen as a marketing device, intended to raise Dior's public profile with the bringing in of a flamboyant media star who sports a bullfighter's moustache, Rasta braids and outrageous clothing.
Arnault, who launched the fashion house of the intensely imaginative designer Christian Lacroix, also controls Celine, Kenzo and Guerlain perfumes.

When Galliano was first named at Givenchy, the fashion press had talked of his exuberant nightlife, unpredictability and volatile artistic temperament, predicting he would not have the discipline to last at Givenchy.
But his collections have won rave reviews.

Born in Gibraltar, Galliano's family moved to the south London suburb of Battersea in 1966. He was admitted to the prestigious Central St Martin's School of Art and Design in London where he majored in clothing design.
